name: Text as a whole
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulation (EU) 2021/1119 establishing the framework for achieving climate neutrality
part_text:
The European Parliament wants to update the European Union's climate law. It keeps the goal of cutting net greenhouse gas emissions by 90% by 2040 compared with 1990 levels. Countries could cover part of that cut with credits bought from climate projects abroad, up to 5% of 1990 emissions, starting in 2036. The Parliament also asks the Commission to report more often on progress, to consider fairness for industry, farmers and households, and to delay the new emissions trading system for buildings and road transport until 2028.

- The 2040 target stays at 90%, with up to 5% allowed from international credits from 2036.
- It affects industry, farmers, households and countries' climate plans, and delays the new carbon market for buildings and transport to 2028.
- Next, the Parliament and the Council of ministers negotiate the final text.
